A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VinePPO research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial rewriting and relocation of material.

before.justification: v1 reports original MATH and GSM8K experiments with RhoMath 1.1B and DeepSeekMath 7B, including benchmark results, ablations, timing measurements, and value-prediction analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional RLOO/GRPO comparisons, critic diagnostics, rollout-count timing results, and credit-assignment examples.

M1.justification: Both versions replace PPO's critic with Monte Carlo value estimates, compute stepwise advantages, and assign each reasoning step's advantage to its tokens. Auxiliary rollouts remain excluded from direct policy training. Section 4 is clarified and rewritten without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use MATH and GSM8K for mathematical reasoning. The added diagnostics and examples remain within this coverage; no additional dataset, domain, or distinct task scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: RLOO and GRPO, previously discussed but not experimentally compared, become evaluated baselines across both datasets and model sizes. v2 includes them in performance, generalization, and runtime comparisons in Figures 4–6, while retaining PPO, DPO+, and RestEM.

E3.justification: v2 adds explained variance as a critic diagnostic and specifies protocols for the new RLOO/GRPO experiments, including KL-coefficient tuning and a selected coefficient of 3e-3. Existing dataset splits, model sizes, Pass@1 evaluation settings, and PPO/VinePPO hyperparameters remain unchanged. Expanded descriptions of existing sampling budgets do not establish that those experiments changed.

E4.justification: v2 adds an analysis addressing critic undertraining through explained-variance and MAE trajectories (Appendix D.2), extends the existing rollout-count ablation to wall-clock efficiency (Figure 7b), and adds three credit-assignment case studies (Appendix E). Existing generalization, KL, temperature, and value-ranking analyses are retained or expanded rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Section 7 newly quantifies uncertainty in the 256-rollout reference values: their Bernoulli sample-mean variance is at most approximately 0.001. The reference sample count is unchanged, and both versions average accuracy over 16 evaluation rounds with different random seeds; no increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial comparator and diagnostic results. For DeepSeekMath on MATH, Figure 4 newly reports RLOO at 36.8% and GRPO at 36.4%, alongside unchanged PPO and VinePPO scores of 42.8% and 46.0%. It also adds rollout-count timing and case-study outcomes. Figure 5 revises the RhoMath/MATH train-versus-test trace from v1 Figure C.4 without explaining the revision; this should not be interpreted as a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Appendix C.5 adds mathematical definitions of GRPO and RLOO advantages and reasoning about baseline dependence and gradient bias. Section 7 adds the Bernoulli variance calculation. The original MDP formulation, PPO/GAE equations, VinePPO estimator, and unbiasedness claim remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims about inaccurate PPO critics and effective Monte Carlo credit assignment remain. v2 extends superiority claims to RLOO/GRPO and newly claims to be the first RL post-training algorithm that scales generalization slope through additional compute. Higher test accuracy at comparable training accuracy was already claimed in v1 Appendix C.7; its promotion to the abstract is not an entirely new finding.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new critic diagnostics as evidence against undertraining and argues that already-capable LLMs justify spending more compute on accurate updates. Appendix E.27 adds a useful qualification: nonzero advantages need not correspond to logically incorrect or insightful steps. The earlier explanations concerning KL efficiency, temperature sensitivity, and errors later in reasoning chains remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds RLOO/GRPO hyperparameters and implementation information, identifies RhoMath across both datasets as the basis for PPO hyperparameter selection, and explains checkpoint loading and separate vLLM engines per GPU rank. Existing hardware, timing tables, software choices, and code/container access statements are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Chang et al., Chu et al., DeepSeek-R1, and Agent Q, while removing several earlier introductory and discussion references. It more explicitly positions the work against methods without stepwise credit assignment and adds the generalization-scaling novelty claim. The established relationships to Vine-TRPO, MCTS, and process supervision remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method explanation, and discussion are extensively rewritten. Results are reorganized around performance, efficiency, generalization, and rollout count; KL and temperature discussions move to the appendix, while the existing generalization analysis moves into the main text. An impact statement is added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 2 is substantially redrawn, comparison plots gain additional methods, diagnostic panels are split or recombined, and numerous existing figures move between the main text and appendices. New diagnostic plots, a baseline hyperparameter table, and illustrated case studies further change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 discussed critic-free RL alternatives without testing them, leaving an important comparative gap. v2 directly evaluates RLOO and GRPO and adds critic-training diagnostics and rollout-count efficiency analysis, substantially strengthening the evidence for VinePPO's practical advantages. Additional implementation details improve reproducibility. The stronger claim about scaling generalization slope is less directly demonstrated than the accuracy and runtime findings, but the improved comparative evidence provides a substantial net quality gain.
